pathway.title: HERC HOLDINGS INC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Scale and customer spread are the main credit support. No customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue, national accounts are 49%, and equipment rental is the only segment, so weakness in one end market is diluted across contractors, industrial, infrastructure and commercial facilities customers. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

- Leverage is the main constraint and is falling through earnings, not repayment. Net debt is 4.12x reported last-twelve-months EBITDA and total debt 4.16x at September 30, 2026, against 3.90x reported by the issuer on adjusted pro forma earnings; the ratio was 4.79x at March 31 and 4.27x at June 30 while carrying net debt at September 30 was only USD 23 million above its March 31 level. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Interest absorbs much of the earnings gain. EBITDA covers cash interest 3.65x over the last twelve months, cash interest paid rose 54.95% in nine months 2026 as the acquisition financing ran for a full period, and the floating-rate revolver and term loan keep it sensitive to rates. Basis: calculation C3; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

- Free cash flow is thin and disposal-dependent. Issuer free cash flow of USD 133 million for nine months 2026 includes USD 345 million of disposal proceeds; before them operating cash flow less capital expenditure is negative USD 212 million, and dividends of USD 71 million take 53.38% of the issuer figure. Basis: calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6

- Liquidity is adequate for now and the nearest refinancing is the AR Facility. Cash plus revolver availability is USD 2,100 million, 3.96x last-twelve-months cash interest; the AR Facility of USD 550 million is fully drawn and due on August 31, 2027, and the largest principal bucket, 45.82% of the December 31, 2025 ladder, falls in 2030. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C14; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

- Governance and financial policy are mixed rather than adverse. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, the dividend of USD 0.70 per share continues and the acquisition was debt-funded; capacity under the debt agreements is unread, so willingness and capacity to extract value are both unevidenced. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53

- Margins face cost pressure that the issuer ties to the acquisition, fuel and delivery. Direct operating expense was 44.63% of equipment rental revenue in nine months 2026 against 42.95%, while the issuer's adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 41.5% from 41.0%. Basis: calculation C16; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- Integration is reported complete but cannot be verified. Management says synergies are tracking to plan, and no integration cost or synergy amount is disclosed, so the earnings gain cannot yet be split between synergies, organic demand and acquired revenue. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-07-28_herc2026q2-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1

runs.text: Strengths are scale, spread and access. Scale and market position are average, with an estimated 4% market share in a fragmented industry; business diversification is strong because no customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue and national accounts are 49%; the ability to refinance is average, supported by the redemption of the 2027 notes at par with new 2031 and 2034 notes and by USD 2.8 billion of 2030 and 2033 notes issued in 2025, but untested by rating or price evidence; liquidity is strong at USD 2,100 million, with the revolver due in 2030. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; calculation C8

Weaknesses are cash generation and cost. Free cash flow stability is weak because issuer free cash flow depends on USD 345 million of disposal proceeds; margin stability and cost flexibility are average, since direct operating expense rose to 44.63% of equipment rental revenue while rent, insurance and overhead are fixed; competitive advantage is average, resting on scale and national accounts rather than contracts, as virtually all rentals can be cancelled within a day; financial policy and governance are average, with a debt-funded acquisition, a continuing dividend and no sponsor to backstop equity. Basis: calculation C9; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On June 2, 2025 Herc completed its acquisition of H&E Equipment Services, a full-service rental company with branches in over 30 U.S. states, for a total purchase price of USD 4.8 billion, made up of USD 2.9 billion of cash and new Herc shares valued at USD 584 million, and paid a further USD 1.4 billion in cash to extinguish H&E debt that was not assumed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C16

Herc funded the deal with USD 2.8 billion of new senior unsecured notes due 2030 and 2033, a USD 750 million term loan and USD 2.5 billion drawn on a new asset-based revolver of up to USD 4.0 billion, of which about USD 1.6 billion repaid the prior revolver, so carrying debt nearly doubled in 2025. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 114–116; calculation C17

In December 2025 Herc redeemed the USD 1.2 billion 2027 notes at par using the proceeds of USD 600 million each of new 2031 and 2034 senior notes, and it cut the term loan margin; the AR Facility was amended four times between August 2025 and August 2026 and now stands at USD 550 million, due on August 31, 2027. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

Herc sold its Cinelease studio entertainment business on July 31, 2025 for USD 100 million of initial cash plus earnouts and used the proceeds to repay debt, and in 2024 it bought the assets of Otay Mesa Sales for about USD 273 million. The documents describe no pending acquisition and no new debt issue after the third quarter of 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: HERC HOLDINGS INC (issuer id hri), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module sets out the business, transaction, ownership, governance and operating facts that matter to creditors, drawn from the seven supplied documents. It makes no recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Herc is a diversified, scaled equipment-rental business whose credit risk now rests on integrating the debt-funded H&E acquisition rather than on its market position; no controlling holder is disclosed and the dividend continues, so creditor protection comes from performance, not sponsor support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition, completed on June 2, 2025 for a total purchase price of USD 4.8 billion, nearly doubled carrying debt in 2025 and added branches in over 30 U.S. states; management says integration finished in the first quarter of 2026 but publishes no integration cost or synergy amount. Demand is spread: no customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue and national accounts are 49%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_herc2026q1-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The USD 0.70 quarterly dividend continued through the acquisition year, and the ownership and compensation detail that would show who controls the company sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business is scaled and diversified, which supports cash-flow resilience through the cycle. Contractors, industrial, infrastructure and government, commercial facilities and other customers account for 38%, 25%, 18%, 14% and 5% of equipment rental revenue, national accounts for 49%, and no customer exceeds 3%. Equipment rental is 86.15% of FY2025 revenue and the only segment, so fleet utilization and rental rates drive almost all earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The H&E acquisition is the dominant credit event, and its delivery matters more than business quality. The USD 4.8 billion purchase was funded by USD 2.8 billion of new senior unsecured notes, a USD 750 million term loan and USD 2.5 billion drawn on a new revolver, and new Herc shares valued at USD 584 million went to H&E holders. Management says integration finished in the first quarter of 2026 and synergies are tracking to plan, but integration cost and synergy amounts are not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership and control give creditors neither a sponsor to lean on nor a sponsor to fear. No holder above reporting thresholds is named, the chairman is non-executive and the annual report incorporates holdings, compensation and related-party detail by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a controlling holder is not ruled out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation is mixed rather than extractive. The dividend of USD 0.70 per share each quarter continued while debt rose, but there were no repurchases in 2025, disposal and refinancing proceeds went to debt, and the 2027 notes were redeemed at par. Dividends paid of USD 71 million in the first nine months of 2026 equal 53.38% of the issuer's free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_herc2026q3-pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leased branches and a fixed cost base amplify cyclical risk. About 94% of locations are leased, operating lease liabilities of USD 1,502 million sit outside debt, rental contracts can be cancelled within a day, and rent, insurance and overhead do not fall in the winter, so a demand slowdown reaches cash flow faster than the revenue mix suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_hri-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating momentum is strong but largely acquired. Equipment rental revenue rose 21.09% in the first nine months of 2026 and dollar utilization reached 43.5% in the third quarter against 39.9%, yet direct operating costs rose to 44.6% of equipment rental revenue in the nine months, and organic growth is not separated from acquired growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Legal exposure looks ordinary-course on the evidence supplied: claims arise from operating rented equipment and workers' compensation, and management does not expect a material adverse effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against treating integration as the main risk is operating: utilization, rental revenue growth and twice-raised 2026 guidance suggest the combined fleet is earning more per dollar of cost, and the near-term notes were replaced at par rather than through an exchange. The view would soften if cross-selling and branch optimization lift margins as management says and synergy amounts are disclosed; it would harden if integration costs recur, organic growth proves weak once acquired revenue is removed, or the dividend and fleet investment are funded by borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The ownership conclusion changes if the proxy statement shows a holder with influence over distributions, because the finding that sponsor extraction risk is absent would no longer hold.

fields.name: Quote

fields.value: On June 2, 2025 Herc completed its acquisition of H&E Equipment Services, a full-service rental company with branches in over 30 U.S. states, for a total purchase price of USD 4.8 billion, made up of USD 2.9 billion of cash and new Herc shares valued at USD 584 million, and paid a further USD 1.4 billion in cash to extinguish H&E debt that was not assumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Herc funded the deal with USD 2.8 billion of new senior unsecured notes due 2030 and 2033, a USD 750 million term loan and USD 2.5 billion drawn on a new asset-based revolver of up to USD 4.0 billion, of which about USD 1.6 billion repaid the prior revolver, so carrying debt nearly doubled in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In December 2025 Herc redeemed the USD 1.2 billion 2027 notes at par using the proceeds of USD 600 million each of new 2031 and 2034 senior notes, and it cut the term loan margin; the AR Facility was amended four times between August 2025 and August 2026 and now stands at USD 550 million, due on August 31, 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Herc sold its Cinelease studio entertainment business on July 31, 2025 for USD 100 million of initial cash plus earnouts and used the proceeds to repay debt, and in 2024 it bought the assets of Otay Mesa Sales for about USD 273 million. fields.value: HERC HOLDINGS INC (issuer id hri), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesises the business, financial and governance evidence into a fundamental credit view. It assigns no rating and makes no recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Herc's fundamental credit profile is adequate: a scaled, diversified fleet business whose net leverage of 4.12x on reported last-twelve-months EBITDA is elevated and falls only through earnings growth, leaving creditors reliant on cash flow, an asset-backed revolver and disposals rather than sponsor support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main support is spread: no customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue, liquidity is USD 2,100 million with USD 2,034 million available under a revolver due 2030, and last-twelve-months EBITDA rose 16.53% from March to September 2026. The main constraint is cash generation: issuer free cash flow of USD 133 million includes USD 345 million of disposal proceeds, and the fully drawn USD 550 million AR Facility matures on August 31, 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a construction slowdown that cuts utilization while rent, insurance and overhead stay fixed, which would raise leverage on flat debt; the monitor is net leverage on reported EBITDA moving above 4.12x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and customer spread are the main credit support. No customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue, national accounts are 49%, and equipment rental is the only segment, so weakness in one end market is diluted across contractors, industrial, infrastructure and commercial facilities customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is the main constraint and is falling through earnings, not repayment. Net debt is 4.12x reported last-twelve-months EBITDA and total debt 4.16x at September 30, 2026, against 3.90x reported by the issuer on adjusted pro forma earnings; the ratio was 4.79x at March 31 and 4.27x at June 30 while carrying net debt at September 30 was only USD 23 million above its March 31 level.

fields.value: - Interest absorbs much of the earnings gain. EBITDA covers cash interest 3.65x over the last twelve months, cash interest paid rose 54.95% in nine months 2026 as the acquisition financing ran for a full period, and the floating-rate revolver and term loan keep it sensitive to rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hri-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

fields.value: - Free cash flow is thin and disposal-dependent. Issuer free cash flow of USD 133 million for nine months 2026 includes USD 345 million of disposal proceeds; before them operating cash flow less capital expenditure is negative USD 212 million, and dividends of USD 71 million take 53.38% of the issuer figure.

fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate for now and the nearest refinancing is the AR Facility. Cash plus revolver availability is USD 2,100 million, 3.96x last-twelve-months cash interest; the AR Facility of USD 550 million is fully drawn and due on August 31, 2027, and the largest principal bucket, 45.82% of the December 31, 2025 ladder, falls in 2030.

fields.value: - Governance and financial policy are mixed rather than adverse. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, the dividend of USD 0.70 per share continues and the acquisition was debt-funded; capacity under the debt agreements is unread, so willingness and capacity to extract value are both unevidenced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margins face cost pressure that the issuer ties to the acquisition, fuel and delivery. Direct operating expense was 44.63% of equipment rental revenue in nine months 2026 against 42.95%, while the issuer's adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 41.5% from 41.0%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Integration is reported complete but cannot be verified. Management says synergies are tracking to plan, and no integration cost or synergy amount is disclosed, so the earnings gain cannot yet be split between synergies, organic demand and acquired revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the earnings trajectory: last-twelve-months EBITDA rose 16.53% in six months, the third-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin reached 44.2%, the issuer raised 2026 guidance for the second time this year and replaced its 2027 notes at par. If net debt stays flat and EBITDA keeps growing, reported leverage would keep falling toward the issuer's 3.90x. The view would improve if free cash flow before disposals turned positive and synergy amounts were disclosed; it would worsen if utilization or rental rates fell, if disposal proceeds weakened, or if the AR Facility were not extended well ahead of August 31, 2027.

fields.value: Strengths are scale, spread and access. Scale and market position are average, with an estimated 4% market share in a fragmented industry; business diversification is strong because no customer exceeds 3% of equipment rental revenue and national accounts are 49%; the ability to refinance is average, supported by the redemption of the 2027 notes at par with new 2031 and 2034 notes and by USD 2.8 billion of 2030 and 2033 notes issued in 2025, but untested by rating or price evidence; liquidity is strong at USD 2,100 million, with the revolver due in 2030.

fields.value: Weaknesses are cash generation and cost. Free cash flow stability is weak because issuer free cash flow depends on USD 345 million of disposal proceeds; margin stability and cost flexibility are average, since direct operating expense rose to 44.63% of equipment rental revenue while rent, insurance and overhead are fixed; competitive advantage is average, resting on scale and national accounts rather than contracts, as virtually all rentals can be cancelled within a day; financial policy and governance are average, with a debt-funded acquisition, a continuing dividend and no sponsor to backstop equity.
